subject: dsa
title: Koko Eating Bananas
summary: Binary-search the answer, not the input. Feasibility is monotonic in speed, so search speeds 1..max; for each, check if the total hours fit, and narrow toward the slowest that works.
problem: Koko eats one pile per hour at speed k, taking ceil(pile/k) hours per pile. Find the smallest k that finishes all piles within h hours.

steps.caption: Koko eats one pile at speed k bananas/hour, taking ceil(pile/k) hours each. Find the slowest k that clears piles [3,6,7,11] within h = 8 hours.
A higher speed never needs more hours, so feasibility is monotonic. Binary-search the speed over [1, 11] (11 = the largest pile).
Test mid = 6: hours = 1+1+2+2 = 6 <= 8. Feasible — 6 works, but maybe a slower speed does too.
Since 6 works, drop every speed above it and search the lower half, [1..5].
Test mid = 3: hours = 1+2+3+4 = 10 > 8. Too slow — 3 and anything slower can't finish in time.
Test mid = 4: hours = 1+2+2+3 = 8 <= 8. Feasible! Look for something even slower.
Nothing slower than 4 works, so the minimum eating speed is 4 bananas/hour.
